# Parley v0.1.55

Two things: a terminal type choice for remote hosts, from Mark's report on
19 September 2026, and the GitLab pipeline moved into throwaway Tart macOS
VMs. Built and verified on 19 September 2026.

## Terminal type for remote hosts

Parley's embedded Ghostty advertises `TERM=xterm-ghostty` and ships that
terminfo entry, so programs on the Mac find it. A remote host reached over
ssh has no such entry unless it was installed there: ncurses programs
refused to start with `ncurses: cannot initialize terminal type
($TERM="xterm-ghostty")`, and the delete key stopped deleting and moved the
cursor instead, because the host could not look up which byte the key
sends.

- **Settings › Terminal › Terminal type** offers **Ghostty**
  (`xterm-ghostty`, the default, which changes nothing) and **Compatible**
  (`xterm-256color`, which every host knows).
- The choice applies to shell and agent panes started or restarted
  afterwards. A running pane keeps the value it launched with; Parley never
  restarts a pane for this. Container panes always receive `xterm-256color`
  from Docker and are untouched.
- The value travels as one `TERM=` word for `/usr/bin/env` inside the
  launch command, read once per launch generation. It is deliberately not
  put into Ghostty's surface environment, because Ghostty applies its own
  `term` option on top of that environment.
- Settings and Help show Ghostty's own remedy for keeping the Ghostty type
  on a server, `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty | ssh <host> -- tic -x -`, with a
  Copy button. Parley never runs it. Help's troubleshooting topic names
  the exact error.

## GitLab jobs in Tart VMs

Every pipeline job now runs in a throwaway macOS VM on the self-hosted
`macos` runner through the Tart custom executor: a digest-pinned
`ghcr.io/cirruslabs/macos-tahoe-base` image, the checksummed nodejs.org
Node build on an explicit PATH, `glab` installed by the release job, and
nothing surviving between jobs. The VM has no Docker runtime, so both
jobs leave the two Docker-only deterministic checks out with an explicit
`--skip` on `parley-native-checks`, which prints one `SKIP` line per check
and counts them in the summary. `npm test` is now composed of
`npm run test:checks` and `npm run test:scripts` plus the two scans so a
pipeline can pass that argument, and the contract tests pin the skip list
to those two names.

## Verification

The merge request's pipeline ran in the VM: all 377 native checks passed
with the 2 Docker-only checks reported as skipped, 54 script tests, both
repository scans and the native build. Eight new checks cover the terminal
type: the launch shape for shell and every host vendor, the restart-only
application, the container launch keeping Docker's value, a real Ghostty
surface reading `$TERM` for both choices, and the remote failure reproduced
locally with Ghostty's terminfo out of reach. The Help audit pins the new
Settings and troubleshooting text. The setting has not yet been exercised
by hand against a remote host; the manual scenario is in
`docs/test-scenarios.md` under Terminal behaviour. Unnotarized beta, as
before.
